why: A shopping centre exit survey of 8,000 visitors whose visit-reason split (53/25/22) and film-type pie (31/17/20/14/11/7) each add to 100% is believable.
A bindery putting 0.5 FTE on 55 albums a month (about 1.5 hours an album) and adding two binders to reach 2.5 FTE for 262 June albums is consistent and plausible.
49 to 131 newspaper copies per person a year, 20 to 60 pages a copy, and cover prices of EUR 0.8 to 2.0 above unit costs of EUR 0.3 to 0.7 are believable national figures.
A music store chain with about 330 to 400 million in revenue across four activities and margins of 3% to 31% (highest for lessons) is believable.
A garden centre chain with 264 to 313 million in revenue and department margins of 6% to 25% (highest for the cafe) is believable.
Each office's sector split adds to 100%, and the hours per head (about 1,600 billed hours a year per person in every office) are plausible for an engineering consultancy.
Print and online profits add to the stated totals each year, and margins of 0.5% to 3.0% imply sales of about 0.8 to 1.2 billion in local currency, believable for a regional newspaper group.
Airport projects costing $26m to $40m upfront and $300k to $450k a month, adding 1,900 to 5,500 passengers a day at $6 to $9 profit each, are believable for a busy regional airport.
The price and volume parts add to each product group's total, and the groups sum to about 3.3 percentage points of average annual revenue growth, believable for a packaged food maker.
7,000 exit-survey respondents over four weeks at a seaside aquarium, with two pies that each add to 100%, is believable.
